newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money unchanged, sellers emerge.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money unchanged, sellers emerge.

text.p: Manila overnight money remained at 10.03125 percent in a liquid market on Wednesday, with rates moving from 10.25 to 10.03125 percent.
Market volume was still high at 14.301 billion pesos from 13.469 billion pesos, reflecting the high liquidity in the market, traders said.
However, more sellers of T-bills emerged at the secondary market after the lukewarm response to yesterday's sales of seven-year T-bonds, traders said.
The auction of seven-year T-bonds was undersubscribed with tenders totalling 3.34 billion pesos against planned sales of 3.5 billion pesos.
"We've hit a resistance at these levels," a dealer said.
"Interest rates are seen bottoming out," a second dealer said, adding banks are now taking profits.
A Reuter poll of six financial institutions gave offer rates of 9.70 to 9.75 on three-month bills, 10.0 to 10.10 percent on the six-month bills, and 10.45 to 10.50 percent for the one-year bills.
